ideas.title: Icom Just Filed Two New VHF Digital Radios With the FCC: What We Know
ideas.why_now: Icom filed two VHF digital transceivers with the FCC on 2026-10-14, plus a VHF air band transceiver on 2026-10-08. Filings often show up before an announcement, and our audience follows Icom closely after the ID-5200.
ideas.angle: Fits the 2026-10-22 YouTube slot, the most time-sensitive opening. Walk through what is actually public in the filings, compare it to the ID-5200 we already covered, and clearly label anything speculative (a filing is not a product yet). New angle versus the earlier Retevis and Radioddity filing pitch: this is Icom, the brand behind most of our best results. Cut a Short with the one most interesting detail.

ideas.title: eBay's New Radio Listing Rules: Buying and Selling Ham Gear After the FCC Change
ideas.why_now: New FCC rules on online electronics sales took effect, and eBay responded by restricting radio transmitter listings while exempting ham-band-only gear. It lands right before holiday buying season and winter hamfest swap tables.
ideas.angle: Record 2026-11-03 for the 2026-11-05 podcast slot. Segments: what changed and what is exempt, what it means for used and vintage gear, how to vet a used or returned radio before you pay, swap meets and auctions as alternatives, and listener questions. Practical buyer and seller advice, not legal hand-wringing. Exception note: used gear alone has a low competitor breakout rate, so the timely FCC and eBay hook carries this, with brand names up front in the title.

ideas.title: New Shack PC, Silent IC-7300: Getting Audio and WSJT-X Working on Windows 11
ideas.why_now: Logging and software talk is up 1.54x in the last 30 days, and hams upgrading shack computers are hitting missing USB audio devices and broken digital mode setups.
ideas.angle: Fits the 2026-10-29 YouTube slot. Start from a fresh Windows 11 machine, plug in an IC-7300, and show every step: drivers, audio devices, CAT control, WSJT-X, logging hand-off. Show the common failure and the fix on screen. Evergreen how-to with a popular brand in the title, a format we have not done.

ideas.title: Building the QRP Labs QMX+: Toroids, Firmware, and the Mistakes to Avoid
ideas.why_now: Homebrew discussion is up 1.36x with 110 recent posts, and QMX+ builders are asking the same questions this week: how much solder, how to wind T507, firmware loading, and dead-on-arrival builds.
ideas.angle: Fits the 2026-11-12 YouTube slot, good bench content as weather turns. Build the kit on camera, answer the common forum questions as we hit them (T507 windings, solder, firmware), then take it on the air for a first QRP contact. Mention the ferrite bead tip for portable use, but keep the title off POTA since park content underperforms for us.

ideas.title: HTCommander First Look: Testing the Free App on Our Handhelds
ideas.why_now: A video on this free app just hit nearly 4x its channel's typical views, and handheld plus software interest are both rising.
ideas.angle: Fits the 2026-11-19 YouTube slot. Set it up from scratch with one of our handhelds, test which everyday tasks it really handles for us, note setup snags, and say who it is for. Different from the earlier Winlink net pitch: this is a single-app hands-on aimed at handheld owners, including people getting new HTs for the holidays.

ideas.title: Keeping New Hams on the Air: Gatekeeping, Elmers, and That First Contact
ideas.why_now: New-ham talk is up 1.31x, a gatekeeping debate is running hot this week, another podcast just covered online negativity, and ARRL is surveying former members about why they left. New radios under the tree make December the right time.
ideas.angle: Record 2026-12-01 for the 2026-12-03 podcast slot. Fits our non-elitist identity: bring in a recently licensed club member, talk about what actually helped them get on the air, how to answer a nervous first call on a repeater, and how clubs can mentor without scolding. Exception note: Clubs has a low breakout rate, so lead with the new ham framing, which breaks out much more often.
